Two printers in an old kiln workshop on Gojōzaka, Kyoto’s pottery slope. One 1960s letterpress, one risograph that only speaks fluorescent.

Small editions, loud inks, and a weekend where you get your hands dirty.

SaturdayPress 1 of 2

Letterpress

Pick wood and lead type from the cases, set a line in the composing stick — backwards, the way it has always been — lock it in the chase and pull it on the proof press. Mind your p’s and q’s: on the sort they are mirror images.

SundayPress 2 of 2

Risograph

Split your design into two layers, burn a stencil master for each, and run an edition of thirty through the drums — fluorescent pink first, then blue. Where they cross, you get a third colour nobody mixed.

SplitBurnRunStack

Two colour separations, a pink stack of sheets and a blue kiln arch, printed over each other.
